title: OPA‐IF‐SVNF‐MARCOS decision framework and its application to determine the optimal fish species for integration into an aquaponic system
content:
Abstract

The overall success and long-term sustainability of an aquaponic system are heavily dependent on the careful selection of fish species. Each species possesses distinct characteristics in terms of environmental requirements, growth rates, and compatibility with specific plant crops, making the choice of fish a critical factor in determining the system's productivity and operational efficiency. The importance of this selection is further emphasized by its potential to enhance resource utilization, maximize yields, and minimize environmental impact benefits— that can be realized through a well-informed and structured decision-making process. To address this need, the present study introduces a novel hybrid MCDM methodology, termed OPA-IF-SVNF-MARCOS, designed to identify the most suitable fish species for aquaponic systems. In this approach, the OPA-IF component is utilized to determine the priority values of evaluation criteria, while the SVNF-MARCOS method is employed to rank the available alternatives effectively. Additionally, the study includes a comparative evaluation using two well-established MCDM models to benchmark the performance and reliability of the proposed method. Supported by comparative analysis, statistical testing, and sensitivity assessment, the results consistently identify Tilapia as the most suitable fish species for aquaponic systems. Through the application of this hybrid model, Tilapia has emerged as the most favorable fish species for aquaponic integration. The framework for selecting fish species within the aquaponic system contributes significantly to the development of a more sustainable and resilient system. By ensuring ecological balance and compatibility among system components, this approach ultimately enhances the overall productivity and efficiency of the aquaponic setup.
